text: Darby Township Board of Zoning Appeals Public Notice November 2, 2026 The Darby Township Board of Zoning Appeals will hear an appeal on Monday, November 2, 2026 at 6:30pm. The meeting will be held at the Darby Township Hall, 508 4th Street, Unionville Center. Gunnar Teegardin, 17400 Burns Road, Marysville, Ohio is requesting the approval of a zoning variance for the construction of a 30’ x 40’ pole barn for the additional storage of vehicles, personal property, and/or equipment. The two adjacent parcels are a total of 1.172 acres. Currently there is an existing occupied residence and an accessory building on parcel# 07-0003034.0000. There are no structures on parcel# 07-0003034.1000 which is where the proposed pole barn (1,200 sq/ft) will be located. For questions contact: Jackie Ward, Zoning Inspector Phone:614-616-6304 Email: jward@unioncountydarbytwp.com Amy Chapman, BZA/BZC Secretary Phone: 406-240-2221 Email: achapman@unioncountydarbytwp.com

text: COURTYARDS AT EVANS FARM, SECTION 2 Farm Lots 2 of Section 1 Farm Lots 14 of Section 2 Township 3, Range 18 United States Military District Township of Orange, County of Delaware, State of Ohio NOTES 1. Easements are hereby reserved, in, over, and under areas designated on this plat as Drainage Easement or Utility Easement. Easements designated as Drainage Easement or Utility Easement permit the construction, operation, and maintenance of all public and quasi-public utilities above, beneath, and on the surface of the ground and, where necessary, for the construction, operation, and maintenance of service connections to all adjacent lots and lands and for storm water drainage. Reserve "M" that are located alongside the rights-of-way hereby dedicated. Also granted is the right of Del-Co Water Company Inc., to install, service, and maintain water meter crocks and appurtenances in said easement areas alongside said rights-of-way. The easement area shall be for the unobstructed use of Del-Co Water Company, Inc. Placement of fences, walls, pillars, trees, gardens, shrubberies, and other surface features is strictly prohibited. 2. Easements designated as “Sanitary Easement” shall mean an exclusive sanitary easement over, through, under, within, upon, and across the area described on the plat, together with ingress and egress over reasonable routes across Grantor's tracts that adjoin the easement area when exercising the purposes of this easement, exclusively for construction, operation and maintenance of public and or private sanitary sewers, service connections, manholes, force mains, valves, and other sanitary appurtenances. Sanitary easements may be crossed by other utilities as expressed herein. 15. The private drives will be part of a condominium known or to be known as “The Courtyards At Evans Farm Condominium”. The private drives identified on this plat shall be common elements as that term is defined in chapter 5311 of the Ohio Revised Code. As such, the private drives will be jointly owned by all unit owners as tenants-in-common and maintained in perpetuity by an association comprised of the owners of units in the condominium. The private drives associated with this development were not designed or constructed to public road standards, and will not be dedicated as public roads. Neither Delaware County nor Orange Township will be responsible for maintenance, repair or re-construction of the private drives. all residential and other improvements shall and must be part of the aforesaid condominium. No residential structure may be occupied unless and until it complies with the terms and conditions of this note and the structure is made part of the aforesaid condominium. The owner and any subsequent transferee of a lot delineated herein affirmatively waive the right to challenge or appeal the denial of any occupancy permit until that property has been made part of the condominium. 3. Within those areas of land designated “Drainage Easement” on this plat, an additional easement is hereby reserved for the purpose of constructing, operating, and maintaining major storm water drainage swales and/or other above ground storm water drainage facilities. No above grade structures, dams, or other obstructions to the flow of storm water runoff are permitted within Drainage Easement areas as delineated on this plat. Easement areas shown hereon outside of the platted area are within lands owned by the undersigned and easements are hereby reserved for the uses and purposes expressed herein. 4. All easements and reserves that overlap or cover all or portions of a “Sanitary Easement” shall be subject to the provisions of the “Sanitary Easement” within the overlap or cover areas. Work to facilitate surface water drainage within the overlap or cover areas is not restricted; however any proposed new storm sewer pipes, inlets, catch basins, structures, or other storm water appurtenances or infrastructure features subsequent to those which were permitted with the original sanitary sewer improvements shall only be permitted if approved by the governing stormwater authority and the Delaware County Sanitary Engineer. 5. For any easement shown on this plat that contains a storm sewer, culvert, over land open ditch flood route, detention basin, retention basin and/or other storm water structure (herein referred to as storm sewer), the storm sewer rights are senior to the rights of any other public or private utility or interest utilizing the easement, except for overlap areas with a “Sanitary Easement”. Any costs associated with the damage, repair, replacement or relocation of any buried or above ground facility or structure that is necessary to allow the maintenance, repair or replacement of the storm sewer shall be the responsibility of the owner of said utility, facility or structure. When maintenance, repair or replacement of a storm sewer causes the removal of any trees, plantings, landscaping, fence, driveway or any other feature located within the easement, the replacement and cost of said items shall be the responsibility of the owner of the underlying property or homeowner's association if applicable. 6. Any landscape features, such as trees, fences, retaining walls, etc. in drainage easements shall be reviewed by the Delaware Soil and Water Conservation District (DSWCD) and the Delaware County Engineer's Office (DCEO) prior to installation. The DSWCD and DCEO will review the proposed improvements to assure that the improvements will not interfere with the storm water control facilities. 7. No other utility lines, conduits, mains, valves, boxes, pedestals, transformers, or other utility appurtenances are permitted within any Sanitary Easement unless they are approved on the signed sanitary sewer plans, or otherwise approved in writing by the Delaware County Sanitary Engineer, except that the rights granted to Delco Water Company, its successors, and assigns to install, service and maintain residential water services, meter crocks and appurtenances as designated on this plat are not restricted. 8. Other utility crossings within the Sanitary Easement are only permitted as described herein, unless they are approved on the signed sanitary sewer plans or otherwise approved in writing by the Delaware County Sanitary Engineer. Right angle or near right angle utility crossings (“near right angle” is defined as an angle between eighty (80) degrees and one-hundred (100) degrees) over, across, or under a sanitary sewer or force main and over, across, under, or through the sanitary easement are not hereby restricted, except that all utility crossings under a sanitary sewer or force main shall be subject to the review and approval of the Delaware County Sanitary Engineer. 9. No buildings, sheds, decks, pools, or other such structures, or the footers or foundations of any structures or features shall be constructed above or below ground within the limits of the Sanitary Easement unless said structure is approved in writing by the Delaware County Sanitary Engineer. 10. Any landscaping features, such as, but not limited to, trees, fences, signs, stackable retaining walls, etc., within the Sanitary Easement shall be reviewed for approval by the Delaware County Sanitary Engineer prior to installation. 11. When maintenance, repair or replacement of public sanitary sewers, manholes, force mains, valves, and other public sanitary appurtenances causes the removal of any trees, plantings, landscaping, fence, or any other feature located within the Sanitary Easement, with the exception of driveways and pedestrian pathways, the replacement and cost of said items shall be the responsibility of the owner of the underlying property or homeowner's association if applicable. 16. Approval of this plat by the Delaware County Regional Planning Commission, the Delaware County Commissioners and/or any other government authority shall in no way constitute a dedication or acceptance of the private street shown thereon, and all such private street(s) shall be and remain a private access way. The Delaware County Regional Planning Commission, the Delaware County Commissioners and every other public authority signing this plat shall have no responsibility or liability for or arising out of the construction, improvement, maintenance and/or use of any such private street. The owners of these lots and their successors and assigns agree to and shall be bound by the foregoing provision, which provision shall be deemed to be and is a covenant running with the land. 17. Reserves E, G, and M will be part of a condominium known or to be known as “The Courtyards At Evans Farm Condominium”. Reserves E, G, and M identified on this plat shall be common elements as that term is defined in chapter 5311 of the Ohio Revised Code. As such, Reserves E, G, and M will be jointly owned by all unit owners as tenants-in-common and maintained in perpetuity by an association comprised of the owners of units in the condominium. Motion ___ 2ND ___ Roll ___ November 4, 2026 2 CLICK HERE FOR CASE INFORMATION RESOLUTION NO. 2026-089 Board of Trustees, Liberty Township Butler County, Ohio RESOLUTION TO [ACCEPT/MODIFY/OVERTURN] THE RECOMMENDATION OF THE LIBERTY TOWNSHIP ZONING COMMISSION NOTICE OF DECISION FOR CASE ZC26-019, BRENT WILKINS, ON BEHALF OF M/I HOMES OF CINCINNATI, LLC, AND TO [APPROVE/DENY] A ZONING MAP AMENDMENT FROM RA-1 (RESIDENTIAL-AGRICULTURAL DISTRICT) TO R-PUD (RESIDENTIAL PLANNED UNIT DEVELOPMENT DISTRICT) FOR AN 88.0545ACRE SITE AND A PRELIMINARY PUD PLAN CONTAINING 110 SINGLE-FAMILY RESIDENTIAL LOTS RESOLVED by the Board of Township Trustees of Liberty Township, Butler County, Ohio that, WHEREAS, Brent Wilkins, on behalf of M/I Homes of Cincinnati, LLC, submitted an application requesting a Zoning Map Amendment from RA-1 (Residential-Agricultural District) to R-PUD (Residential Planned Unit Development District) for an 88.0545-acre site and a Preliminary PUD Plan containing 110 singlefamily residential lots; and WHEREAS, on October 19, 2026, the Liberty Township Zoning Commission conducted a public hearing for the proposed request and recommended denial; and, WHEREAS, a public hearing was conducted by the Liberty Township Board of Trustees on Wednesday, November 4, 2026 at 6:00 p.m. for the proposed Zoning Map Amendment from RA-1 (Residential-Agricultural District) to R-PUD (Residential Planned Unit Development District) for an 88.0545-acre site and a Preliminary PUD Plan containing 110 single-family residential lots; and, WHEREAS, all those present for the hearing who wished to be heard voiced their opinions with respect thereto; and, WHEREAS, said application was reviewed by the Board of Township Trustees and determined it to be [consistent/inconsistent] with the Liberty Township Comprehensive Plan; now, THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that the Liberty Township Board of Trustees do hereby [accept/modify/overturn] the recommendation of the Liberty Township Zoning Commission and [approve/deny] the request for a Zoning Map Amendment from RA-1 (Residential-Agricultural District) to R-PUD (Residential Planned Unit Development District) for an 88.0545-acre site and a Preliminary PUD Plan containing 110 single-family residential lots, subject to the details listed in the staff report, all attached exhibits, and as modified by the following conditions: 1. At no time shall any structure be permitted within the 80’ wide Texas Gas Easement, which includes principal and accessory structures, fences, etc. unless written approval is obtained from the easement holder. 2. A Traffic Impact Study (TIS) shall be required, which shall be submitted to the Butler County Engineer’s Office (BCEO) for their review and shall be subject to their approval. All recommendations of the TIS and traffic concerns from the BCEO shall be addressed accordingly and incorporated into the Preliminary PUD Plan and all Final PUD Plans. If a TIS is not required for this development, written documentation from the BCEO shall be provided to Liberty Township. 3. The appropriate right-of-way shall be dedicated pursuant to the Butler County Thoroughfare Plan. 4. The final design of the access points onto Millikin Road shall be subject to approval by the BCEO and Final PUD Plan approval. 5. On-street parking shall be limited to one side of the opposite of the fire hydrants. The required fire hydrants shall be coordinated with the Liberty Township Fire Department. 6. A typical street section shall be provided, which shall include concrete curb and gutters. All public roadways and sidewalks shall be constructed according to the BCEO Subdivision Regulations, and all private roadways shall be constructed to the same public road standards. 7. The public roadway stub (Road A) to the south shall be provided as illustrated on the Preliminary PUD Plan. 8. Sidewalks and asphalt paths shall be designed in accordance with the BCEO standards and shall include a 5’ wide sidewalk on both sides of all public and private roads, including along Millikin Road, and shall be constructed of concrete. The internal “pedestrian path” through the open space shall be a minimum of 6’ wide with an asphalt surface, which shall Liberty Township Resolution 2026-089 2/6 be provided as they are illustrated on the Preliminary PUD Plan. However, during Final PUD Plan review, the sidewalk along the Millikin Road frontage shall be evaluated, which currently terminates at Road D, to determine if any additional improvements should be made to extend the sidewalk further east toward the rail line/bridge that may include grading considerations for a future sidewalk and/or installation of additional sidewalk. 9. The Miami-2-Miami Regional Trail Network and the Liberty Township Trails Plan shall be considered during Final PUD Plan review, which shall include coordination from Liberty Township, Butler County and related trails planning agencies, to determine if this regional trail should be located on the east or west side of Gregory Creek. If it is determined that the regional trail should be located on the east side of Gregory Creek, the following modifications should be made to the path design and alignment: the trail should enter the property at the northwest corner of the site along Millikin Road and travel along Millikin Road to Road C, then continue along Road C and extend into the open space parcel behind Lots 106-110 where it would tie into the proposed path; then, the trail should extend to the south property line near Pond 3. Additionally, the proposed 6’ wide asphalt pedestrian path shall be widened to 10’ to match the width of the trail alignment in Turnbridge/Cherokee Park/Shannon Ridge. Final details of the trail connections shall be reviewed at the Final PUD Plan stage, if approved. 10. A detailed grading and drainage plan shall be provided with all Final PUD Plans, which shall demonstrate how the stormwater is being handled for the site according to the Butler County Storm Water Regulations. All retention ponds shall include a water feature or aeration device to preserve good water quality. 11. Setbacks shall be approved according to the Preliminary PUD Plan for each lot type; however, all front yard setbacks shall be evaluated during Final PUD Plan review to ensure consistency throughout the subdivision, especially on the south and west side of Road B along Lots 85-99. Liberty Township Resolution 2026-089 3/6 12. The following building material standards shall apply for all single-family residential structures for the Orchard Walk R-PUD: a. Front elevations shall be brick and/or natural stone for all primary vertical planes (those supported by the foundation). The use of Faux Stone, MDO Smooth Face Laminate trimmed with Primed Redwood, Shakes (hardi-, cement, wood, or vinyl), Hardi-Plank or Cem-Plank siding (masonry based product) and Architectural Composite Trim Materials (i.e. Fypon) or other approved materials of equal quality are permitted as alternative materials for architectural features, such as Bay Windows (box and neo-traditional), Detail Gable Projections, Window Gables, and select features where brick/masonry cannot be supported. b. Side and rear elevation shall be brick and/or natural stone for the entire 1st story. Extensions on the 1st floor, such as fireplaces and bay windows may be sided using Hardi-Plank or Cem-Plank siding (masonry based product). Areas above the 1st story may be sided using Hardi-Plank, Cem-Plank, or premium vinyl siding no less than .44 mils thick. c. Building additions, including enclosed sunrooms, shall be held to the same building material requirements as listed above and constructed using materials matching the house. 13. A detailed landscape plan shall be provided at the Final PUD Plan review, which shall include the following: a. Millikin Road: Street trees are typically required at a rate of one tree every 40 feet and equally spaced and aligned; however, Millikin Road is categorized as a ‘Major Collector’ within the Butler County Thoroughfare Plan and Section 8.4.1(2)(a) of the Liberty Township Zoning Resolution requires an earthen mound that varies in height but has an average height of six feet. Street trees should be provided at a rate of one tree per 10 feet, which should be staggered near the top of the mound and shall be a mixture of deciduous and evergreen trees. A detailed grading and landscape plan should be required with the Final PUD Plan for the buffer mound along Millikin Road. b. East Buffer: A buffer should be provided along the Norfolk Southern Rail Line, which should include the proposed 50’ wide open space area and trees at a rate of one tree every 40 feet and equally spaced and aligned. Liberty Township Resolution 2026-089 4/6 c. South Buffer: A 50’ wide open space area is proposed to the south. The closest house to the south is approximately 914 feet away. d. West Buffer: A substantial buffer should be provided along the northern half of the western project boundary as an existing single-family residence sits approximately 115’ from the project boundary. This buffer should be evaluated with the Final PUD Plan to determine if the existing vegetation can serve as a meaningful buffer or if additional plantings should be provided. e. Internal Streets: Street trees should be provided at a rate of one tree every 40 feet and equally spaced or aligned. 14. The Final PUD Plan shall include details for the two main entrances from Millikin Road, the overlook, disc golf course and all other open space amenities, which shall include quality design, landscaping and amenities for an upscale development, which shall be subject to the Zoning Commission approval. 15. The location and design of the entry monument sign and mail kiosk (CBU) shall be reviewed with the Final PUD Plan. 16. All open space and storm water facilities shall be governed by Covenants and Restrictions, and the maintenance shall be the responsibility of the Homeowner’s Association. Open Space and landscaping shall be maintained regularly in accordance with the Zoning Resolution. 17. All comments and concerns of all other agencies shall be addressed to the agency’s satisfaction, which shall be reflected accordingly on the Final PUD Plan. text: App. No. 080-2026 TA Zoning Text Amendment Homer Township Meeting: Applicant: Hearing: Amendments: November 4, 2026 Homer Township Zoning Commission (ZC) October 13, 2026 Table of Contents Article II Definitions Article VI Sign Regulations/Definitions Reviewer: Denise Testa Recommendation: APPROVE Proposal: Mary Cuchna, Zoning Secretary for Homer Township, requested a review of proposed revisions to the portions of the above Homer Township Zoning Resolution (Resolution). The proposed amendments revise sign regulations to remove the existing text addressing billboards. Staff recommend modifications to ensure consistency with the Ohio Revised Code (ORC) while preserving the Township's ability to regulate outdoor advertising in a content-neutral manner that supports its aesthetic objectives. The page numbers identify where the proposed text appears within the Resolution. TABLE OF CONTENTS Page 4 SIGN REGULATIONS ARTICLE II Page 10 DEFINITIONS ARTICLE VI SIGN REGULATIONS Section 601-1 Page 63 Definitions Section 601-3 Signs For Home Occupations And Conditionally Permissible Uses In The R-1 And R-2 Districts Page 64 Section 601-6 Page 66 ___ ___ Billboards/Outdoor Advertising With the exception of Section 601-3, Staff reviewed these text amendments in August 2026, as documented in the attached staff report. Based on that review, Staff finds the proposed amendments associated with this application to be warranted. Department of Planning Services Recommendation: Staff recommend the Medina County Planning Commission Approve the proposed text amendments to the Homer Township Zoning Resolution. Attachement: August 2026 Homer Township Text Amendment Staff Report App. No. 048-2026 TA Zoning Text Amendment Homer Township Meeting: Applicant: Hearing: Amendments: August 5, 2026 Homer Township Zoning Commission (ZC) July 14, 2026 Article II Definitions Article VI Sign Regulations/Definitions Reviewer: Denise Testa Recommendation: APPROVE WITH MODIFICATIONS Proposal: Mary Cuchna, Zoning Secretary for Homer Township, requested a review of proposed revisions to the portions of the above Homer Township Zoning Resolution (Resolution). The proposed amendments revise sign regulations to remove the existing text addressing billboards. Staff recommend modifications to ensure consistency with the Ohio Revised Code (ORC) while preserving the Township's ability to regulate outdoor advertising in a content-neutral manner that supports its aesthetic objectives. The page numbers identify where the proposed text appears within the Resolution. ARTICLE II Pages 1 and 8 DEFINITIONS Comments regarding definitions appear under Section 601-1. ARTICLE VI SIGN REGULATIONS Section 601-1 Page 1 Definitions See comments below. Section 601-5 Page 4 Section 601-6 Page 5 Business Signs Billboards/Outdoor Advertising The proposed text amendment eliminates the definition of billboards and adds text referencing the ORC 519.20. ORC Section 519.20 classifies outdoor advertising as a business use. The ORC states that, “…outdoor advertising shall be classified as a business use and be permitted in all districts zoned for industry, commerce, or trade, or lands used for agricultural purposes.” Because the ORC also mentions “lands used for agricultural purposes,” Staff recommend the Township clarify the zoning district and add language to the Resolution as follows, “These signs are permitted only in the B-1 Business District and lands used for agricultural purposes.” Homer Township Text Amendments Removing the definition may create ambiguity regarding what constitutes an off-premises sign and may inadvertently conflict with ORC 519.20. Rather than removing the definition, staff recommend updating it to a modern definition of "Off-Premises Sign" and revising the regulations to maintain consistency throughout the resolution. If the Township plans to revise its Regulations, Staff recommend replacing the "billboard" definition with a broader, more contemporary definition such as: Off-Premises Sign: An off-premises sign that advertises or directs attention to a business, product, service, event, activity, or location that is not located on the same lot as the sign. Section 601-7 Page 5 Enforcement (renumber) No comment. The Township has sent the text amendments to the Prosecutor. Department of Planning Services Recommendation: Staff recommend the Medina County Planning Commission Approve with Modifications the proposed text amendments to the Homer Township Zoning Resolution. Planning Commission Page 2 of 2 August 5, 2026

title: CHATHAM TOWNSHIP TEXT AMENDMENT, 084-2026 TA
text: App. No. 084-2026 TA Zoning Text Amendment Chatham Township Meeting: Applicant: Hearing: Amendments: November 4, 2026 Chatham Township Zoning Commission (ZC) TBD Article 4 R-1 Residential and Agricultural District Article 5 R-2 Residential and Limited Commercial District Article 8 Conditional Zoning Certificates Reviewer: Denise Testa Recommendation: APPROVE WITH MODIFICATIONS Proposal: Gail Miller, Zoning Secretary for Chatham Township, requested a review of proposed revisions to the portions of the above Chatham Township Zoning Resolution (Resolution). The page numbers identify where the proposed text appears within the Resolution. The proposal establishes conditional zoning certificate requirements, occupancy limits, inspections, renewal periods, property management and contact requirements, and penalties for Short-Term Rentals. ARTICLE 4 R-1 RESIDENTIAL AND AGRICULTURAL DISTRICT Section 402(B)(8) Page 24 Conditionally Permitted Uses (Add #8) No comment. ARTICLE 5 R-2 RESIDENTIAL AND LIMITED COMMERCIAL DISTRICT Section 502(B)(19) Page 29 Conditionally Permitted Uses No comment. ARTICLE 8 R-2 RESIDENTIAL AND LIMITED COMMERCIAL DISTRICT Section 807 Specific Standards Pertaining To Short-Term Dwelling Rentals And Short-Term Owner-Occupied Dwelling Rentals Page 48 Staff recommend the Township reconsider the proposed occupancy limit based on twice the number of bedrooms recorded by the Medina County Auditor. Auditor records may not reflect the current configuration or legally established bedroom count of a dwelling. The Township should clarify how bedroom counts will be verified and how the occupancy limit will be established and documented as part of the conditional zoning certificate. Staff recommend the Township consider whether additional operational standards are necessary to address the potential impacts of short-term rentals on neighboring properties and residential Chatham Township Text Amendments character. The proposed amendments address occupancy and special events; however, they do not establish specific standards for parking, noise, trash collection, or property maintenance. The Township should determine whether these issues are adequately addressed by existing zoning provisions or whether additional standards are warranted. Staff recommend the Township clarify the prohibition on special events and parties, including how the restriction applies when the number of attendees exceeds the permitted occupancy limit. The amendment should distinguish between overnight occupancy and the total number of people present on the property and establish a clear, enforceable standard. Staff recommend the Township clarify how violations are documented and counted for purposes of certificate revocation under Section 807(J). The amendment should establish how the Township determines that a violation has occurred, whether an opportunity to correct a violation is provided, and how the revocation process relates to the penalty provisions in Section 807(I). Renumbering the subsequent sections does not require Planning Commission review. ARTICLE 13 Page 65 DEFINITIONS Staff recommend the Township clarify the definitions of Short-Term Dwelling Rental and ShortTerm Owner-Occupied Dwelling Rental to ensure the two categories are distinct and collectively address the types of rental arrangements the Township intends to regulate. The definition of Short-Term Owner-Occupied Dwelling Rental should clarify whether the primary resident is required to remain on the premises during the rental period. Staff recommend these amendments be reviewed by the Medina County Prosecutor. Department of Planning Services Recommendation: Staff recommend the Medina County Planning Commission Approve with Modifications the proposed text amendments to the Chatham Township Zoning Resolution. Planning Commission Page 2 of 2 November 4, 2026

title: Change Document
text: CHATHAM TOWNSHIP AMENDMENT TO ZONING RESOLUTION 2026 This draft amendment is to add zoning resolution language related to governance of Short-Term Rentals within the township. DEFINITIONS: The below are newly added definitions. Short-Term Dwelling Rental – Any dwelling that is rented in its entirety for less than thirty (30) consecutive days by persons other than the primary resident, from which the primary resident, owner, or other interested party receives monetary compensation and the primary resident is not present and personally living on the premise during the time of the rental. Short-Term Owner-Occupied Dwelling Rental – Any dwelling of which a portion is rented for less than thirty (30) days by persons other than the primary resident, from which the primary resident, owner, or other interested party receives monetary compensation. Below is an amendment to an existing definition: Dwelling, Single-Family- A free-standing building designed for or used exclusively for residence purposes by a single housekeeping unit, with sleeping facilities, permanently installed cooking facilities, and lawfully required sanitary facilities. ADD #8 SECTION 402 (B) CONDITIONALLY PERMITTED USES SECTION 402 PERMITTED USES B. Conditionally Permitted Uses 8. Short-Term Dwelling Rentals and Short-Term Owner-Occupied Dwelling Rentals subject to the provisions of Section 807. ADD #19 TO SECTION 502 CONDITIONALLY PERMITTED USES SECTION 502 PERMITTED USES B. Conditionally Permitted Uses 19. Short-Term Dwelling Rentals and Short-Term Owner-Occupied Dwelling Rentals subject to the provisions of 807. [CONTINUED ON NEXT PAGE] 1 THE SECTION BELOW IS NEWLY ADDED LANGUAGE, SPECIFIC TO SHORT-TERM RENTALS. SECTION 807 SPECIFIC STANDARDS PERTAINING TO SHORT-TERM DWELLING RENTALS AND SHORT-TERM OWNER-OCCUPIED DWELLING RENTALS In addition to the general standards set forth in Section 805, the Board of Zoning Appeals shall also consider whether the application for a conditional use complies with the specific standards for uses set forth herein. A. MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS: At a minimum, approval of a Conditional Zoning Certificate shall require the following conditions: 1. BEDROOMS All bedrooms must be located in a dwelling unit; 2. CAPACITY LIMIT The maximum allowable occupancy shall not exceed more than 2 times that total number of bedrooms as recorded by the Medina County Auditor. 3. CONFIRMATION OF CONDITIONS OF 1 & 2 ABOVE Prior to a hearing for application or reapplication for a Conditional Zoning Certificate, the Chatham Township Zoning Inspector shall ensure that conditions “1” and “2” have been met and shall testify at the hearing outlining the satisfactory inspection of each condition; 4. CONTACT The property owner/operator of the short-term dwelling rental and/or shortterm owner-occupied dwelling rental shall provide the township zoning department with up-to-date contact information so that the township can promptly reach the property owner/operator at any time, whether the owner/operator is on or off the property, to address any issues with the short-term rental property. The property owner/operator must promptly notify the township in the event of any change in contact information; 5. SPECIAL EVENTS No special events, weddings, family reunions, graduation parties, or other parties are permitted where the number of people exceeds the maximum number of occupants permitted, when such event is organized or attended by any renter of the short-term dwelling rental or short-term owneroccupied dwelling rental; and B. TERM The Conditional Zoning Certificate for any such use permitted under this section shall be valid for a period of three (3) years, expiring on December 31st of the third (3) year. The property owner must apply every three (3) years to renew the Conditional Zoning Certificate. The certificate may be reissued if the Board of Zoning Appeals finds that the use has been operated in compliance with the township Zoning Resolution and the prior Conditional Zoning Certificate. If needed, the Board of Zoning Appeals may impose additional conditions for continued operation of the short-term dwelling rental or short-term owner-occupied dwelling before re-issuing the certificate. Failure to secure a Conditional Zoning 2 Certificate by January 1st of the year constitutes a violation of the township Zoning Resolution. If the initial permit application is submitted on or after December 1st, the permit will remain valid for that December, and the three-year permit term will begin on January 1 of the following year. C. RENEWAL Applications for renewal of a Conditional Zoning Certificate shall be submitted during the renewal period, which opens no earlier than ninety (90) days and no later than thirty (30) days before December 31st of the year in which the certificate expires. Failure to file a renewal application within this renewal period may result in expiration of the certificate on December 31st, unless otherwise approved by the Board of Zoning Appeals. D. CHANGE OF OWNERSHIP Any change in ownership of the dwelling unit shall void the Conditional Zoning Certificate and shall require submission and approval of a new Conditional Zoning Certificate within 30 days after the transfer of ownership is recorded with the Medina County Auditor. E. TRANSFER OF CERTIFICATE Transfer of a Conditional Zoning Certificate is prohibited. F. POSTING OF CERTIFICATE The current Conditional Zoning Certificate must be prominently posted inside the dwelling unit and on any hosting platform(s) or in any other advertisement regarding the dwelling unit. G. PROPERTY MANAGER A designated property manager shall be identified who may be the property owner of the short-term dwelling rental and/or the short-term owner-occupied dwelling rental, or the property owner’s agent. The designated property manager shall be available to the township 24 hours per day to ensure that the property is maintained and operated as required by this Zoning Resolution. H. VIOLATIONS: Any of the following will be considered a violation of the Chatham Township Zoning Resolution: 1) Failure to secure a Conditional Zoning Certificate for a short-term dwelling rental or a short-term owner-occupied dwelling rental is considered a violation of the Chatham Township Zoning Resolution 2) Failure to update information with the Township Zoning Department such as the designated contact person, property manager, or property owner’s contact information in a timely manner. 3) Advertising a short-term dwelling rental or a short-term owner-occupied dwelling rental for a capacity in excess of that allowed under the Conditional Zoning Certificate issued by the township. 3 4) Failure of the permit holder or his/her designated contact person/agent to be available at any time during the tenure of an active short-term dwelling rental or a short-term owner-occupied dwelling rental. 5) Providing false or misleading information on the application for a Conditional Zoning Certificate for a short-term dwelling rental or a short-term owneroccupied dwelling rental. 6) Failure to comply with any of the standards under Section 807. I. NUISANCE PER SE. Any Short-Term Dwelling Rental or Short-Term Owner-Occupied Dwelling Rental permit holder, property owner, and/or their designated property manager shall be responsible for an infraction of the Chatham Township Zoning Resolution and shall be subject to a fine of not more than $500.00 for each offense. The township shall have the right to commence a civil action to enforce compliance with this resolution. Each day this zoning resolution is violated shall be considered a separate violation. J. REVOCATION The township may revoke a Conditional Zoning Certificate issued for a short-term dwelling rental or a short-term owner-occupied dwelling rental following two (2) separate violations on the same dwelling unit/property under the same ownership within any single calendar year. The property owner may reapply for a Conditional Zoning Certificate, under this section, the following calendar year and receive such certificate if all violations have been resolved. The following sections have been renumbers as described below. Only the section numbers have changed and everything else remains the same. title: Zoning Resolution
text: Homer Township Zoning Resolution Article II-Definitions ARTICLE II - DEFINITIONS Accessory Use - is a use customarily incidental and subordinate to the principal use or building, located on the same lot or premises as the principal use or building. Accessory Structure - A structure detached from a principal building located on the same lot and customarily incidental and subordinate to the principal building use, and shall comply in all respects with the requirements of this Resolution. (Eff. 5/26/2010) Agriculture – shall be defined by Ohio Revised Code (ORC) Section 519.01 (Eff. 6/27/14) Alteration - as applied to a building or structure, is a change or rearrangement in the structural parts or in the exit facilities, or an enlargement, whether by extending on a side or by increasing in height, or the moving from one location or position to another. Animal Hospital - (See Veterinary Clinic) Auction House – an enclosed place or establishment conducted or operated for compensation or profit as a private or public market where items are offered for sale through competitive bidding. The term “auction house” shall not include on premises estate, foreclosure, real estate or personal property sales conducted upon the estate, foreclosed or For Sale property or property belonging to the personal property owner. The term “auction house” shall not include flea markets, yard sales, or livestock markets defined or regulated elsewhere, or Sheriff’s or bank repossession sales. (Eff. 2/25/16) Basement - is a story, suitable for business or habitation, partially below the level of the adjoining street or ground and below the first tier of floor beams or joists. When a basement floor is less than two (2) feet below the average grade, it will be rated as the first story or ground floor. Bed and Breakfast Home - a dwelling that provides 1 to 4 rooms (limited to two (2) persons or one (1) family per unit/room) for occasional paying guests on an overnight basis for periods not to exceed 7 days, with breakfast being available on premises at no additional cost. A Bed and Breakfast Home is allowable only in a building originally constructed as a one-family dwelling. Billboard - is a "sign" which directs attention to a business, commodity, service, or any other activity conducted, sold, placed, or otherwise offered elsewhere than on the premises on which the billboard is located. Billboards shall be regarded as buildings or structures within the meaning of this Resolution. Boarding House or Rooming House - is a dwelling where meals or lodging and meals are provided for compensation to two (2) or more persons by pre-arrangement for definition periods. A boarding house is to be distinguished from a hotel. -1- Homer Township Zoning Resolution Article II-Definitions Buffer - an area within a property or site generally adjacent to and parallel with the property line, either consisting of natural existing vegetation, or created by the use of trees, shrubs, fences, and/or berms, designed to limit continuously the view of, and/or sound from, the site to adjacent sites or properties. (Eff. 1/14/2000) Building - is a structure designed, built or occupied as a shelter or roofed enclosure for persons, animals or property, and when separated by a firewall, each such separated portion of such structure shall be deemed a separate building. Building, Earth Sheltered - A structure built underground and beneath a continuous exterior surface grade, having a floor at or above the exterior grade on one or more sides. Building Height - is the vertical dimension measured from the average elevation of the finished lot grade at the front of the building, to the highest point of ceiling of a mansard roof; and to the average height between the plate and ridge of a gable, hip or gambrel roof. Building Line - is a line defining the minimum front, side and rear yard requirements. Building, Principal - is a building housing the principal activity performed on any lot. Centralized Sewer System - is where individual lots are connected to a common disposal system whether publicly or privately owned and operated. Centralized Water System - is where individual lots are connected to a common distribution system whether publicly or privately owned and operated. Density - is the number of families residing on, or dwelling units developed on, an acre of land. Dwelling, One-Family - is a detached building designed for, or converted or occupied exclusively by one family. Dwelling, Two-family - is a detached building designed for, or converted or occupied exclusively by two families, living independently of each other. Energy Generating Devices (Wind and Solar) (Eff. 10/27/2010) a. Wind Energy Conversion Systems (WECS) – wind powered rotating devices located on top of a pole or structure that in turn rotates a turbine to generate electricity. b. Small Wind System – a WECS that has a maximum capacity of 100 kilowatts or less and has a maximum height of 140 feet. -2- Homer Township Zoning Resolution Article II-Definitions c. Wind Turbine Height – The height of a wind turbine measured from natural grade to the tip of the rotor blade at its highest point, or blade-tip height, or to the highest point of a vertical axis turbine. d. Wind/Solar Facility – All equipment, machinery, and structures utilized in connection with the conversion of wind or solar energy to electricity. This includes, but is not limited to, towers, transmissions, storage, collection and supply equipment, substations and transformers. e. OFFICIAL ZONING MAP INTERPRETATIONS OF DISTRICT BOUNDARIES RULES OF CONSTRUCTION SECTION 101 TITLE This Zoning Resolution shall be known as the Chatham Township Zoning Resolution. SECTION 102 AUTHORIZATION The authority for establishing “The Chatham Township Zoning Resolution” is derived from Chapter 519.00 of the Ohio Revised Code. SECTION 103 PURPOSE In order to promote and protect the health, safety, and general welfare of the residents of the unincorporated area of Chatham Township, Medina County, Ohio; to preserve the rural character of the Township; to control populations density; to protect and preserve property values; and to insure orderly growth and development in said township in conformance with the adopted Chatham Township Comprehensive Plan, the Board of Township Trustees found it necessary and advisable to adopt a comprehensive plan of zoning which will regulate the location, height, bulk, number of stories, and size of buildings and other structures; percentages of lot areas which may be occupied; building setback lines; size of yards and other open spaces; use of buildings and other structures; uses of the land for trade, industry, residence, recreation, or other purposes, and for such purposes to divide the unincorporated area of Chatham Township into districts and to provide for the administration and enforcement of such regulations. SECTION 104 VALIDITY AND SEPARABILITY It is hereby declared to be the legislative intent that, if any provision(s) of the Zoning Resolution, or the application thereof to any zoning lot, building, or other structure, or tract of land, are declared by a court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid or ineffective in whole or in part, or to be inapplicable to any person or situation, the effectiveness of such decision shall be limited to the provision or provisions which are expressly stated in the decision to be invalid or ineffective, or to the zoning lot, building, or other structure, or tract of land immediately involved in the controversy. All other provisions of this Zoning Resolution shall continue to be separate and 7 Chatham Township Zoning Resolution fully effective, and the application of any such provision to other persons or situations shall not be affected. SECTION 105 REPEALER All existing Zoning Resolutions of Chatham Township, Medina County, Ohio, inconsistent herewith, are hereby repealed. SECTION 106 EFFECTIVE DATE This Zoning Resolution shall become effective from and after the date of its approval and adoption, as provided by law. SECTION 107 INTERPRETATION In interpreting and applying the provisions of this Zoning Resolution, they shall be held to be the minimum requirements for the promotion of public health, safety, morals, comfort and general welfare. Whenever the requirements of this Zoning Resolution are at variance with the requirements of any lawfully adopted rules, regulations, ordinances or resolutions, the most restrictive, or that imposing the higher standards shall govern. SECTION 108 A. B. C. D. E. F. APPLICATION OF REGULATIONS Buildings or land shall hereafter be used or occupied only in conformance with the provision of this Zoning Resolution. Any building or structure or part thereof erected, moved, altered, restored or reconstructed shall hereafter be established and used only in conformance with the regulations herein specified for the district in which it is located. Any building hereafter erected, used, occupied, altered, restored or reconstructed shall comply with this Zoning Resolution in regard to the use, area of lot occupied, and the size of front, rear and side yards. Every new lot shall comply with the minimum required dimensions for lot area, frontage, and lot width for the district in which it is located. No yard or lot existing at time of passage of this Zoning Resolution shall be reduced in dimension or area below the minimum requirements set forth herein. Any part of a yard or other open space required around any building for the purpose of complying with the provision of this Resolution shall not be included as a part of a yard or other open space similarly required for another building. Whenever a boundary line of a district is changed by Amendment of this Zoning Resolution so as to transfer an area from one district to another district of a different classification, the regulations for the district to which said area is transferred shall apply to all buildings, structures, and uses in the area so transferred except for prior legal nonconforming uses, structures, and lots as provided in this Zoning Resolution. A review and recommendation by the Chatham Township Zoning Commission shall be required for any building, structure or use other than: 1. An agricultural building for which a certificate of agricultural use has been executed and filed with the Zoning Inspector; or 8 Chatham Township G. H. I. J. K. L. Zoning Resolution 2. A new single-family dwelling, addition to an existing single family dwelling, or a permitted accessory building on an existing building lot of record in the Residential R-1 District. Every lot shall have frontage upon a public road, or upon a private road approved for frontage, conforming to the requirements of this Zoning Resolution. Not more than one dwelling unit shall be permitted on any individual lot. Any accessory use, building, or structure shall be permitted on a lot or parcel. The use of camping trailers, other types of camping vehicles or equipment, or recreational and/or seasonal facilities, such as cabins or lodges, or house trailers or mobile homes for residence or dwelling unit purposes is prohibited. It shall be unlawful to use land and/or buildings in any district for use which creates a nuisance or which is noxious, dangerous, or offensive by reason of odor, dust, smoke, gas, noise, fumes, flame, vibration, insects or vermin. Pursuant to Section 3796.29 of the Ohio Revised Code, the cultivation, processing, and retail dispensing of medical marijuana is prohibited within Chatham Township. SECTION 109 ESTABLISHMENT OF DISTRICTS For the purposes set forth in this Zoning Resolution, the land area within the unincorporated area of Chatham Township is hereby divided into the following districts: R-1 R-2 Residential and Agricultural District Residential and Limited Commercial District Only those uses specifically identified as being either a permitted principal use, a conditionally permitted use, or an accessory use in a particular zoning district may be permitted in that zoning district. Any use not specifically listed as a permitted, conditional, or accessory use in a zoning district shall be considered a prohibited use in the zoning district. SECTION 110 OFFICIAL ZONING MAP The zoning districts and their boundary lines are indicated upon the map entitled, “Official Zoning Map - Chatham Township, Medina County, Ohio.” Said map is made part of this Zoning Resolution. The said Official Zoning Map, once signed by two or more trustees and dated, together with all notations and references thereon are hereby declared a part of this Zoning Resolution. The original map shall be maintained in the administrative offices of Chatham Township, and shall show thereon all amendments or changes made hereafter. The Zoning Inspector shall be responsible for adding amendments and changes adopted by the Township Trustees to the Official Zoning Map. SECTION 111 INTERPRETATION OF DISTRICT BOUNDARIES The following rules shall be used to determine the precise location of any zoning district boundary unless such boundary is specifically indicated on the Official Zoning Map: 9 Chatham Township A. B. C. D. E. F. Zoning Resolution Where district boundary line is shown to approximately follow a lot line; such lot line shall be construed to be the boundary line. Where a district boundary line is shown as approximately parallel to the right-ofway line of a street or highway, the district boundary line shall be construed as being parallel thereto and at a distance therefrom as indicated on the Official Zoning map. Where the boundary of a district follows a stream, lake or other body of water, said boundary line shall be deemed to be at the high water line. Where the boundary of a district follows a railroad line, such boundary shall be deemed to be located in the middle of the main tracks of the railroad line. Whenever any street, alley, or other public way is vacated, the zoning district adjoining each side of such street, alley, or public way shall automatically be extended to the center of such location, and all areas within that location shall thenceforth be subject to all regulations appropriate to the respective extended district. If no measurement is given, dimensions shall be determined by the use of the scale shown on the Official Zoning Map. SECTION 112 RULES OF CONSTRUCTION For the purposes of this Resolution, certain terms or words herein shall be construed or defined as follows: A. The present tense shall include the “future”, the singular number shall include the “plural” and the plural number shall include the “singular”. B. The word “shall” is a mandatory requirement, the word “may” is a permissive requirement, and the word “should” is a preferred requirement. C. The word “person” includes a corporation, firm, partnership, association, organization, trust or company as well as an individual. D. The word “building” shall include the word “structure”. E. The word “lot” includes the word ‘plot” or “parcel”. F. The words “used” or “occupied” includes the words “intended, designed or arranged to be used or occupied”. G. When the number of days is specified, it shall mean calendar days unless specifically stated otherwise. 10 Chatham Township Zoning Resolution ARTICLE 2 ADMINISTRATIVE POWERS AND DUTIES Section 201 ZONING INSPECTOR Section 202 POWERS AND DUTIES OF THE ZONING INSPECTOR Section 203 ESTABLISHMENT AND PROCEEDINGS OF THE ZONING COMMISSION Section 204 POWERS AND DUTIES OF THE ZONING COMMISSION Section 205 ESTABLISHMENT AND PROCEEDINGS OF THE BOARD OF ZONING APPEALS Section 206 POWERS AND DUTIES OF THE BOARD OF ZONING APPEALS SECTION 201 ZONING INSPECTOR A Zoning Inspector designated by the Board of Township Trustees shall administer and enforce this Resolution and perform such other duties as may be delegated by the Board of Trustees. The Zoning Inspector may be provided with the assistance of such other persons as the Board of Township Trustees may direct. The Township Zoning Inspector, before entering upon his/her duties, shall give bond as specified in Section 519.161 of the Ohio Revised Code. SECTION 202 POWERS AND DUTIES OF THE ZONING INSPECTOR For the purpose of this Resolution, the Zoning Inspector shall have the following duties and powers: A. Accept and review applications for all required permits as set forth in this Zoning Resolution. B. Issue zoning permits and certificates of zoning compliance as provided by this Zoning Resolution and keep a record of the same with a notation of any special conditions involved. C. Deny the issuance of a zoning certificate in those cases where one (1) or more applicable provisions of this resolution are not complied within the application thereto. D. Maintain in current status the Zoning Resolution and Official Zoning Map, which shall be filed with the Medina County Recorder and kept on permanent display in the Township. E. Maintain permanent and current records required by this Resolution including but not limited to zoning permits, certificates of zoning compliance, inspection documents, and records of all variances, amendments, conditional uses, and similar uses. text: Geotechnical Report Discussion Bohaty Planned Development Medina Township Meeting: App. No.: Applicant: Owners: Engineer: Parcels: Site Area: November 4, 2026 026-2026 R Pride One Construction OH Medina Stonegate LLC Davey Resource Group 026-06C-17-027 76.7615 acres Sublots: Block: Zoning: Utilities: School: Reviewers: 74 B UR Urban Residential Central water and sanitary sewer Medina City Denise Testa EXECUTIVE SUMMARY At the October 2026 Medina County Planning Commission (MCPC) meeting, the MCPC Approved with Modifications the Bohaty Replat No. 2 pending completion of the CTL Conclusions outlined in the Geotechnical Peer Review dated October 19, 2026. For MCPC consideration, the attached analysis addresses the shallower groundwater/seepage conditions identified in the CTL peer review for Sublots 20/21. The MCPC requested confirmation whether the proposed slope modifications and building locations continue to provide the appropriate factors of safety. RECOMMENDATION: APPROVE At the October 2026 MCPC meeting, CTL identified a groundwater/seepage condition that was not incorporated into the Wertz slope stability model. Specifically, the Wertz analysis modeled a piezometric line at elevation 900.0, while the B-15 and B-16 boring logs documented moist to wet soils at approximately elevations 911.0 to 915.5. CTL therefore recommended that Wertz re-evaluate the slope stability with the shallower groundwater/seepage conditions included in the model and resubmit the analysis for review. Wertz Engineering submitted the attached report dated October 13, 2026, and CTL completed a Peer Review on October 19, 2026. DPS Recommendation: Planning Services agrees with CTL's conclusion that further evaluation is unnecessary. Staff recommend that the Planning Commission accept and approve the Bohaty Planned Development Replat No. 2 conclusions of the geotechnical peer review prepared by CTL Engineering, dated October 19, 2026, and require compliance with the revised slope stability recommendations provided by Wertz Geotechnical Engineering, dated October 13, 2026. The recommendations include regrading the backyards of Sublots 20 and 21 to reduce the soil mass along the ravine crown, maintaining the recommended setbacks for the homes and foundations, and directing stormwater away from the ravine. An experienced geotechnical engineer shall be present during construction to observe the regrading and make any necessary adjustments based on actual site conditions. CTL has reviewed the revised slope stability analyses and concurs with the proposed approach and recommendations. Attachments: Bohaty Replat No. 2 Wertz Geotechnical Engineering Slope Stability Analysis-October 13, 2026 CTL Engineering Peer Review-October 19, 2026 Dept. of Planning Services Page 2 of 2 November 4, 2026 Pride One Construction 2211 Medina Road Suite 100 Medina, OH 44256 October 13, 2026 Attention: Ben Weinerman RE: Bohaty Property (Stonegate Subdivision), Lots 20 & 21, Calistoga Circle, Medina Township, Medina County, Ohio; WGE #20251060 Mr. Weinerman: The Medina County Department of Planning Services recommended that a slope stability analysis be performed for Lots 20 and 21 of the subject subdivision. The rear slope behind the homes is approximately 55 feet high with an overall inclination of 2.5:1 (horizontal:vertical). The Rocky River is located at the toe of the slope. The hummocky slope surface of the ravine indicates shallow, historic slope failures. The upper 15 to 20 feet of the ravine is steeper, at approximately a 2:1 grade. A subsurface evaluation for the development was performed by WGE with a report of our findings sent to Ben Weinerman of Pride One Construction on April 23rd, 2025. Test Borings B15 and B-16 were performed near the slope on Lots 20 and 21. The subsurface conditions at Boring B-16 & B-18 mostly encountered stiff to very stiff, brown to gray, lean clay. A soft to medium stiff clay layer was encountered in Boring B-15 in the 33.5 to 35.0 feet sampling interval. A loose silt with minor clay was encountered in Boring B-16 in the 33.5 to 35.0 feet sampling intervals. The stability of the existing slope was evaluated using the program Geostase by Gregory Geotechnical Software. Slope stability was calculated using the Spencer Method at specified boundaries (defined arc entry and exit points along the slope surface). The soil shear strength parameters were estimated from field and lab data. See attached slope evaluation package for details. The following summary of our analysis is provided below: • Existing Conditions: The calculated factory of safety (FS) for potential slope failure affecting the backyard area is approximately 1.2. • Proposed Regrading: Additional analyses were performed to evaluate the effects of lowering and reshaping the crown of the ravine. The modeled profiles included cuts of approximately 5 feet to reduce the soil weight along the crown by approximately 20,000 lbs. per linear foot. The results indicate that regrading the crown with a 5-foot cut would Page 1 Stonegate Lots 20& 21 WGE: 20251060 increase the FS for the backyard slope to be greater than 1.3, while the FS for the potential slope failure affecting the home would be approximately 1.5 • For this evaluation, a minimum FS of 1.3 is required for slopes not supporting structures, while 1.5 is required for slopes supporting structures. CONCLUSION Based on the results of our analyses, we recommend re-grading the backyards of Lots 20 and 21 to reduce the soil mass along the crown of the ravine and improve slope stability. The crown should be lowered to Elevation 941, corresponding to an approximate cut depth of 5 feet, over a distance extending from approximately 100 feet south of the common property line between Lots 19 and 20 to approximately 20 feet north of the common property line between Lots 21 and 22. The regraded surface should rise westward away from the ravine at a maximum grade of 8H:1V. The finish grades of the backyard should be field verified by our personnel. As indicated in our engineering letter dated July 16, 2026, the home should be located 35 feet from the existing crown of the ravine. The foundations should be set back at least 50 feet from the slope face, measured horizontally at the foundation bearing elevation. The storm water from home and impermeable surfaces areas should be directed away from the ravine. We hope you will find this report satisfactory. Please contact our office if we can be of further service or you have questions regarding this submittal. Respectfully submitted, Leroy Wertz, P.E. The applicant proposes 143 sublots between 0.83 and 1.2 acres leading to two permanent cul-de-sacs. RECOMMENDATION: APPROVE WITH MODIFICAITONS ADJACENT ZONING/LAND USE Direction Zoning North R-R Rural Residential District East South West R-R Rural Residential District C-1 Commercial District R-R Rural Residential District R-R Rural Residential District Proposal: The applicant proposes 143 sublots for single-family homes with central sewer and water, 91+acres of open space in five blocks, and six stormwater retention ponds. Access: Access to the site is through two connections on Center Road (SR 303) leading to six public streets and five permanent cul-de-sacs. Site Conditions: Most of the planned site is used for agriculture in open fields. A stream and woodlands are located in the southeast portion and two wetlands in the central portion of the site. The site includes six abandoned oil or gas wells. Land Use Single-Family Residences Single-Family Residences Liverpool Township Offices Single-Family Residences Agriculture Single-Family Residence Valley Ridge Estates Preliminary Plan Liverpool Township Development Policy Plan: The proposed subdivision is consistent with the 2015 Liverpool Township Development Policy Plan’s Goal 2 which seeks to “promote the rural atmosphere of the Township while providing for balanced growth.” The site is designated for residential use on the Future Land Use Map, and the proposed subdivision conforms to this planned land use classification. Liverpool Township Zoning Resolution: According to the Liverpool Township Zoning Resolution (ZR), the purpose of R-R Rural Residential district is to provide for rural residential development at a low density which will promote the continuation of the predominant rural residential character of the Township. Where central sewer and water are available, it is the intention of this district to provide for low density residential development at a density of one (1) acre per dwelling unit. To ensure that existing and planned sewer and water facilities are most efficiently utilized, the one (1) acre per dwelling unit density will not be permitted outside the planned service areas as indicated in the Liverpool Township Development Policy Plan. The ZR indicates the purpose of the Controlled Density Zoning (CDZ) Overlay District is to, “...promote the preservation and protection of the rural atmosphere of the Township while providing for anticipated residential development. To accomplish that purpose, Controlled Density Zoning encourages the permanent preservation of relatively large tracts of land (consisting of, but not limited to, open natural areas, woodlands, greenway systems, wildlife habitats, flood plains, agricultural lands, wetlands, and waterways) of the Rural Residential District. These provisions and requirements are established as alternatives to a number of the residential lot requirements found elsewhere in the Resolution. Reductions permitted in these requirements are in exchange for the permanent preservation of open space and other natural features that can benefit not only the residents of the development but the general population of the Township.” Agency Comments: Italicized text indicates agency comments. text: Variance Request and Preliminary Plan White Oak Estates Granger Township Meeting: App. No.: Applicant: Engineer: Parcels: November 4, 2026 077-2026 V-PP Pulte Group, Inc. Cunningham & Assoc., Inc. 005-07B-16-028/032/033 005-07B-22-056 Site Area: Sublots: Zoning: Utilities: School: Reviewer: 100.46 acres 38 Sublots R-1 Residential District On-Site Septic and Private Wells Highland Local Denise Testa EXECUTIVE SUMMARY The 100+ acre site is located south of Interstate 271 (I-271), north of Remsen Road and west of State Road. The applicant proposes 38 sublots and one open space block on public streets leading to permanent public cul-de-sacs. The applicant has requested a variance to Section 604(B)(9) Street Stubs and Cul-de-sacs of the Medina County Subdivision Regulations (Regulations) which states that a permanent culde-sac street shall not exceed 2,500 feet in length. The Planning Commission will need to vote on each item separately. VARIANCE RECOMMENDATION: APPROVE PRELIMINARY PLAN RECOMMENDATION: APPROVE WITH MODIFICATIONS ADJACENT ZONING/LAND USE Direction North East South West Zoning R-1 Rural Residential R-1 Rural Residential R-1 Rural Residential R-1 Rural Residential Proposal: The applicant proposes the following to be completed in two phases: • 38 sublots ranging between 2 and 5+ acres for single-family homes; • 3+ acres of open space; • Two public streets leading to two permanent cul-de-sacs; • Two stormwater management basins with one also functioning as a fire pond; • 25-foot riparian setback for all undisturbed wetlands; and • Wetland impacts of 0.3540 acres. Land Use Residential/Deciduous Forest/I-271 Residential/State Road Residential/Deciduous Forest/Remsen Road Cropland/Residential White Oak Estates Variance and Preliminary Plan Access: Access to the site is proposed at State Road creating two public streets that lead to two permanent public cul-de-sacs. Site Conditions: The site has rolling topography, with elevations generally decreasing toward the drainage features located through the southern portion of the property. A mapped stream extends generally from west to east through the southern portion of the area shown on the aerial map. Areas of wooded vegetation and lower-lying ground are associated with this drainage corridor. The site includes abandoned gas wells on proposed Sublots 9, 13, 16, 23/24, 28, 31 and the Open Space Block. Sublot 25 includes a culvert. Several wetland and surface-water features are mapped within and adjacent to the subject property. These include wetland areas and ponds concentrated along the existing drainage corridor, as well as additional ponds and wetland features on adjacent properties. The aerial mapping also depicts wooded areas associated with portions of the drainage system. The subject property is located within the Rocky River drainage basin. The local drainage system includes Allard Creek, which flows to the East Branch Rocky River. In summary, the subject parcels consist of a combination of open agricultural land, wooded areas, rolling terrain, and areas associated with existing streams, drainage features, wetlands, and surface water. The location and extent of these existing physical features are depicted on the aerial and environmental maps included with this report. Granger Township Zoning Resolution The site is zoned R-1 Rural Residential District. According to the Granger Township Zoning Resolution (ZR), the purpose of the R-1 Residential District “…is to manage low-density residential development that will preserve the rural residential character of Granger Township.” The minimum lot size is two acres and the minimum required frontage is 175 feet. The ZR does not require riparian setbacks and does not include a conservation development option for the R-1 District. Staff recommend the applicant consult with the Township Zoning Inspector to ensure compliance with the ZR and confirm the applicable review/approval procedures. Dept. of Planning Services Page 2 of 8 November 4, 2026 White Oak Estates Variance and Preliminary Plan VARIANCE REQUEST 1. Variance Request The applicant has requested a variance from Section 604(B)(9), Street Stubs and Cul-de-sacs, of the Medina County Subdivision Regulations (Regulations), which limits the length of a permanent cul-de-sac street to 2,500 feet. The proposed length of Wojtowicz Way is 3,643 feet, representing an increase of approximately 46 percent over the maximum permitted length, while the proposed length of Cannata Way is 2,920 feet, representing an increase of approximately 17 percent. 2. Site Conditions and Access Considerations. The Granger Township Zoning Inspector has indicated that the Township prefers that access to the subdivision be provided solely from State Road. Although the property has frontage on Remsen Road, establishing an additional access point would require disturbance of the existing creek and could impact the rural character of the area. Staff note that the requested variance allows the subdivision to be designed in a manner that minimizes environmental impacts while accommodating the Township’s preferred access arrangement. 3. Variance Criteria Section 203(A)(2) of the Regulations establishes the criteria for granting variances. Staff comments regarding compliance with these criteria are provided below: a. The MCPC must find that an unnecessary hardship may result from the strict application of the Regulations due to exceptional topographic or other conditions. The combination of the site’s physical characteristics, the presence of the creek, and the Township’s preference for a single access point from State Road creates circumstances that limit roadway design options. Requiring strict compliance with the 2,500-foot standard would likely necessitate additional roadway connections or a significant redesign of the subdivision layout, resulting in greater environmental disturbance. The requested variances represent an approach that balances site constraints with the overall objectives of the Regulations. b. The MCPC may vary the Regulations to relieve an established hardship, provided such relief can be granted without detriment to the public interest and without impairing the intent and purpose of the Regulations or the desirable development of the neighborhood and community. The Regulations state that the cul-de-sac length limitation is intended to promote “greater convenience to traffic, more effective police and fire protection, and efficiency of road maintenance.” The Granger Fire Department has no concerns about the proposed street lengths on the permanent cul-de-sacs. Based on the information submitted, the proposed street lengths do not appear to adversely affect internal traffic circulation or roadway maintenance. Granting the variance would not appear to impair the intent and purpose of the Regulations or the desirable development of the subdivision and surrounding area. Dept. of Planning Services Page 3 of 8 November 4, 2026 White Oak Estates Variance and Preliminary Plan c. The Regulations provide criteria for determining hardship and granting relief but do not establish specific standards regarding the amount of a variance that may be approved. Over the past 19 years, the MCPC has granted five variances related to cul-de-sac length, with approved increases ranging from approximately 5.6 percent to 37.6 percent above the permitted maximum. The average increase granted was approximately 17.7 percent. The requested variance for Cannata Way is generally consistent with prior approvals, while the requested variance for Wojtowicz Way exceeds the range of past approvals and has been evaluated in the context of the site constraints, environmental considerations, Township access preferences, and comments received from emergency service providers. Recommendation: For further consideration, the applicant has included additional materials in the attached Variance Summary & Exhibits including maps highlighting cul-de-sac street lengths of other Granger Township subdivisions. The Department of Planning Services staff recommend the Planning Commission to Approve both variances for the White Oak Estates Preliminary Plan.
